project.name: breadcrumbs
project.one_liner: BREADCRUMBS is an always-on, on-prem food-safety agent for a NYC food operator: it watches the live FDA recall feed, knows the operator's suppliers and locations, and the instant a recall lands it answers — which of my sites are exposed, how bad, and what to do — in seconds, offline, on an NVIDIA GB10.
project.full_context: BREADCRUMBS is a same-day build for the Dell x NVIDIA AI Factory (BuilderBase) hackathon, Aug 22 2026. The brief: an always-on BUSINESS agent that runs LOCALLY on the GB10 (no cloud inference). BREADCRUMBS is a food-supply risk & recall-response agent scoped to NYC. It monitors the FDA (openFDA) food-recall feed, cross-references a food operator's suppliers and locations, and on a recall computes EXPOSURE (which of my sites received the affected lot), RISK (how bad — using the distributor's real recall history plus the site's real critical food-handling violation history), and ACTION (hold / pull / swap supplier, drafted and fired as an SMS to affected site managers). A local NVIDIA Nemotron agent swarm (Watcher -> Tracer -> Risk -> Briefer -> Comms) does the reasoning, orchestrated via OpenClaw/NemoClaw and reading from a local MongoDB. The wow is the operator's own city rendered in 3D (extruded NYC buildings at real LiDAR heights, reused from the Sixth Borough engine — same deck.gl stack), with exposure glowing on the real blocks, plus live GB10 telemetry proving the reasoning is on the box. WHY LOCAL (load-bearing, not decorative): a buyer's supplier list, margins and sourcing are trade secrets they will never send to a cloud LLM; FSMA 204 makes traceability a legal mandate; always-on + private = only possible on the GB10. INSTRUMENT NOT ORACLE: it reports REAL state (real recalls, real distributor recall history, real critical-violation history, real buildings) and visibly LABELS the modeled parts (supplier->site links, which are proprietary in reality — exactly the FSMA-204 gap — and the operator's illustrative portfolio). No black-box prediction.
hard_rules: LOCAL-ONLY inference at demo time: all model inference runs on the GB10 box on-site (hackathon rule + the product's sovereignty pitch). No cloud API for inference during the demo.

AGENT IS BUILT ON THE DAY: the data pipeline, cached datasets, MongoDB load, and the deck.gl console are pre-built SCAFFOLDS (explicitly allowed by the rules). The AGENT logic (the swarm, its tool-calls, its reasoning) is built during the event. Do not present a pre-finished agent.

AGENT FRAMEWORK = NemoClaw (primary): NemoClaw is NVIDIA's local-agent runtime for Nemotron on the GB10 — sponsor-aligned and the natural fit for local inference; it satisfies the 'at least one of NemoClaw/OpenClaw/OpenShell' rule. OpenClaw is the off-box dev fallback behind the SAME model/agent adapter so the on-box swap is one line. Verify NemoClaw's exact API on the box (day-of).

MONGODB, USED TASTEFULLY (not a dumb JSON store): (1) recalls/establishments/distributors/operator_sites are native heterogeneous DOCUMENTS; (2) a 2dsphere GEOSPATIAL index on all geocoded docs so exposure/blast-radius are real $geoWithin/$near queries; (3) the agent's analytical TOOLS are Mongo AGGREGATION pipelines ($lookup joins recalls<->distributors<->sites, $group for scorecards/compounding) — not hand-rolled JS loops; (4) a CHANGE STREAM on the recalls collection IS the always-on Watcher — a new recall insert fires the swarm. This makes 'always-on + geospatial reasoning' architecturally real.

OFFLINE: every dataset is fetched ONCE and cached to disk / loaded into local Mongo (openFDA recalls, DOHMH inspections, NYS stores, distributor scorecard, NYC buildings). At demo time the whole system runs with the network unplugged. Vendor deck.gl + fonts locally (no unpkg at demo).

REAL vs MODELED, always labeled. REAL: openFDA recalls, DOHMH critical-violation history, distributor recall history, NYC buildings, Comtrade origins. MODELED (label in UI + narration): supplier->restaurant links (proprietary in reality), the operator's portfolio, the covers/day exposure multiplier. Never conflate the two classes.

RISK SIGNAL IS CRITICAL FOOD-HANDLING VIOLATIONS, NOT THE LETTER GRADE. DOHMH letter grades are a composite (vermin, facility, paperwork, temperature). Use the DOHMH critical_flag='Critical' violations (unapproved/unknown source, improper holding temperature, contaminated food-contact surface, vermin in food) as the compounding-risk axis — those are causally linked to whether a site turns a recalled lot into an illness. Do NOT claim a letter grade measures supplier/ingredient safety.

BRANCH + FILE OWNERSHIP (critical — humans build in parallel): this loop runs on branch 'ralph' and edits ONLY backend paths — agent/ sim/ db/ scripts/ bridge/ — plus PRD.JSON and evidence/. NEVER create or edit globe/*.html, globe/assets/*, mockups/, or docs/*; those are HUMAN-OWNED (frontend + assets built by teammates on ui-*/assets-* branches off food). The console consumes the loop's output through bridge/ (Mongo-backed JSON over a documented contract), never the reverse. If a task seems to require editing a human-owned file, stop and write the contract in bridge/ instead.

THE AGENT ACTS. The swarm must make visible, autonomous tool-calls (watch_feed / ingest_recall / trace_forward / score_risk / brief / draft_sms / send). A render-only build fails the 'always-on business agent' brief.

PROVE THE BOX, DO NOT ASSERT IT. A live telemetry HUD (tokens/sec, unified-memory GB of 128, SoC watts of ~140, N agents concurrent) read from NVML/tegrastats — nvidia-smi under-reports on GB10 unified memory. Show multiple agents running concurrently as the hardware flex.
INSTRUMENT NOT ORACLE: report real state; label any simulation; the agent refuses to claim certainty it does not have.
This codebase is written by an AI loop: comments minimal and only where they inform the next iteration; test only what must survive repeated runs; the verification IS the test.

project.scope_locked_aug22: PRIZE-RUN, reliable core. Product = BREADCRUMBS, on-prem NYC food-safety agent. POV = operator's console ('my sites'), city-scale is a toggle. Hero = reactive recall-response. Buyer = generic NYC food buyer, demoed through a restaurant group. Provenance = one origin beat (openFDA firm state + Comtrade commodity origin), NOT the full import graph. SMS = mock phone UI (offline, no creds). The wow = agent swarm + GB10 telemetry + the SMS action, staged on the 3D city. Maritime build is abandoned on branch main as a fallback only.
project.already_built_scaffolds: Real data cached in globe/assets/ (nyc-restaurants 17204 graded, nyc-stores 11224, distributor-scorecard, food-types, food-sources, nyc-nta, manhattan_buildings 45194). Consoles globe/food.html (2D) + globe/food3d.html (3D extruded NYC + risk hexbins + hubs + recall-trace). Fetchers in scripts/. Premise in docs/premise.md. These are ALLOWED scaffolds; the loop builds the agent + Mongo + integration ON TOP.

milestones.name: Preflight + MongoDB load
tasks: scripts/preflight.sh: assert node>=18, python3>=3.10, a local MongoDB is reachable (mongod on localhost:27017), and JS/python deps install into LOCAL envs (never system).

scripts/load_mongo.py: load the cached datasets into MongoDB collections — recalls (openFDA), establishments (DOHMH latest-graded + critical-violation count per camis), distributors (scorecard), buildings_meta (counts only, not the geometry). Idempotent (drop+reload). Provenance stamp per doc: source + fetched_at + class ('real').
Add a critical-violation count per establishment: re-derive from DOHMH critical_flag='Critical' rows (NOT the letter grade). Store crit_violations:int on each establishment doc.

Tag each recall doc: allergens[] parsed from reason_for_recall (undeclared peanut/tree-nut/milk/egg/soy/wheat/fish/shellfish/sesame) + hazard_class (allergen|pathogen|foreign-material|other). Real openFDA text only, no invention. Allergen recalls are ~6,896 — the #2 cause of all food recalls.

Store every geocoded doc (establishments, operator_sites, distributor hubs) with a GeoJSON 'loc' field and build a 2dsphere index on each — so blast-radius/exposure become real $geoWithin/$near queries.

db/queries.py: the analytical primitives as Mongo AGGREGATION pipelines — exposure ($match+$lookup recalls<->distributors<->sites), distributor scorecard ($group), compounding ($match crit_violations>0). These pipelines are what the agent's tools call.
verifications: preflight.sh exits 0 and prints a MongoDB serverStatus ok:1
after load_mongo.py, db.establishments.count() >= 15000 and db.distributors.count() >= 8 and db.recalls.count() >= 300 (E.coli Class-I) — assert via a mongo query script
a random establishment doc has crit_violations (int), a GeoJSON loc, and a 'real' provenance class; a distributor doc has class1 (int) — assert via query
a $near query around a hub returns nearby establishments (2dsphere index is used — assert via explain() index scan), and the exposure aggregation returns the same set as the pure-python control

recalls are allergen-tagged: db.recalls.count({hazard_class:'allergen'}) is in the thousands (matches openFDA ~6,896 for undeclared/allergen); a sample undeclared-peanut recall has allergens containing 'peanut' — assert against a control recall that is pathogen-only and has hazard_class!='allergen'
evidence: V1: scripts/preflight.sh exits 0 and prints 'MongoDB serverStatus ok:1' (mongod on localhost:27017; python3.14 .venv + pymongo 4.17).
V2: db.establishments.count()=17204 (>=15000), db.distributors.count()=10 (>=8), db.recalls.count()=29309 (>=300), Class-I E.coli=349 (>=300) — asserted by scripts/verify_m0.py.
V3: sampled establishment has crit_violations:int, GeoJSON loc Point, provenance.class='real' (source NYC DOHMH 43nn-pn8j); distributor doc has class1:int=205 + provenance.class='real'.

V4: $near around US FOODS hub uses 2dsphere index (explain winningPlan IXSCAN indexName=loc_2dsphere) and returns 5 establishments within 1km; exposure() aggregation == pure-python exposure_control() (parity, operator_sites empty in M0 — both []).

V5: db.recalls.count({hazard_class:'allergen'})=5664 (in the thousands, ~openFDA 6287 undeclared); sampled undeclared-peanut recall has allergens=['peanut']; pathogen-only control has hazard_class='pathogen' with empty allergens.

milestones.name: Operator model — portfolio + modeled supplier links
tasks: sim/operator.py: define the operator's portfolio = ~12 REAL geocoded DOHMH establishments (an illustrative NYC restaurant group; label class:'modeled-portfolio'). Persist to Mongo collection operator_sites.
Assign each site a MODELED primary distributor (nearest-hub rule over the 5 real NYC hubs; store rule + class:'modeled-link'). This is the proprietary edge we cannot get real — label it everywhere.

operator alert-preference profile (the notification layer): {min_severity, scope (suppliers | radius_m), categories[], allergens[] (which allergens the operator cares about), channel (telegram|digest|console), quiet_hours}. matches(recall, profile) -> bool decides whether a recall alerts. Settable in plain English OR as toggles.
exposure(recall) -> the operator_sites whose distributor matches the recall's distributor; deterministic and pure.
verifications: operator_sites has exactly 12 real geocoded establishments, each carrying class:'modeled-portfolio' and a modeled distributor link
exposure() for a Dole-linked recall returns a deterministic, non-empty subset of operator_sites (same input -> identical output across runs)
every modeled doc is tagged class:'modeled-*' — a query proves no modeled doc is mislabeled 'real'

matches(recall, profile) filters correctly: a Class-I allergen recall matching the profile returns True; a Class-III recall outside the profile's categories/allergens returns False (assert both — a filter that lets everything through fails)

milestones.name: Recall-response engine (exposure x risk x action)
tasks: sim/respond.py: given a recall doc, compute EXPOSURE (operator sites via M1), RISK (the distributor's real class1 count + how many exposed sites have crit_violations>0 — the compounding signal), and an ACTION recommendation (hold + swap to the lowest-class1 distributor, e.g. Baldor 0).
Use the recall's REAL product text + reason + firm state for the brief; keep the origin beat (firm state + Comtrade commodity origin) as a supporting field.

If the recall is an allergen recall (hazard_class='allergen'), add allergen_match: the allergen(s) + which of the operator's categories carry that allergen risk (CATEGORY-level, MODELED — per-menu-item matching needs menu data we don't have, label it roadmap).
Emit a structured Response object: {recall, exposed_sites, compounding_count, distributor_risk, allergen_match, recommendation, provenance}.
verifications: for the real Dole leafy-greens Class-I recall, respond.py returns exposed_sites>0, compounding_count = (# exposed with crit_violations>0), distributor_risk.class1 == the real openFDA count, and a swap recommendation naming a 0-class1 distributor
deterministic: same recall doc -> byte-identical Response
the Response carries provenance separating 'real' fields from 'modeled' (exposure via modeled links) — assert the modeled flag is present
for an undeclared-allergen recall, Response.allergen_match names the allergen(s) and flags category exposure labeled MODELED; for a pathogen-only recall, allergen_match is null/empty (control)

milestones.name: Agent swarm (OpenClaw/NemoClaw, tool-calling, concurrent)
tasks: agent/swarm.py via NemoClaw (primary runtime): five roles — Watcher (subscribes to a Mongo CHANGE STREAM on recalls — a new insert fires the swarm; this IS the always-on watch), Tracer (call the exposure aggregation), Risk (call risk scoring), Briefer (compose the plain-language brief), Comms (draft the SMS + supplier hold notice). Each is a tool-calling agent over the M0 aggregation pipelines + M2 functions.
Off-box: model behind an adapter = the OpenRouter default (glm) via OpenClaw so the scaffold is buildable now. On-box (M6): swap to local Nemotron via NemoClaw — one line at the adapter.
Run Tracer/Risk concurrently where independent; log every tool-call (name, args, result) to an evidence transcript.
The Briefer/Comms outputs must be grounded in the M2 Response — no invented numbers; refuse certainty (instrument-not-oracle).
verifications: running the swarm on the Dole recall produces a structured brief whose numbers EQUAL the M2 Response (no drift) — assert by comparing fields
the tool-call transcript shows watch_feed -> ingest_recall -> trace_forward -> score_risk -> brief -> draft_sms in order, with real args/results logged
the model adapter has exactly one place to swap OpenRouter<->local Nemotron (assert the interface exists); at least one of OpenClaw/NemoClaw/OpenShell is the runtime

This is the ONLY interface between the loop-backend and the human-built frontend.

bridge/CONTRACT.md: document every endpoint + JSON shape (field names, types, and provenance class real/modeled) so the frontend team wires globe/food3d.html from the doc alone, without reading backend code.
bridge/samples/: write sample payloads (e.g. the Dole-recall Response) the console can fetch offline. DO NOT edit globe/*.html, globe/assets/*, or mockups/ — those are human-owned.
verifications: GET /response?recall=<dole> (or bridge/out/response.json) returns exposure/risk/action whose numbers EQUAL respond.py (no drift) — assert by comparison
CONTRACT.md documents every field with its provenance class; operator_sites is valid GeoJSON with modeled labels

milestones.name: Comms action — Telegram alert (real) + mock phone fallback
tasks: The Comms agent drafts (a) a short layman alert (SMS-style, <=2 sentences) to affected site managers and (b) a supplier hold notice, both grounded in the M2 Response.

PRIMARY channel = Telegram Bot API: send via a bot token (read from env/config, NEVER committed) to the operator chat_id — a real message lands on a real phone. Sending is I/O, not inference, so it does not violate the local-inference rule.
FALLBACK channel = the mock phone UI in the console: fully offline, no network — for the pull-the-cable moment or flaky venue wifi. The operator alert-preference profile (M1) picks the channel.
The alert text names the real recall, the # exposed sites, the compounding count, and the swap recommendation.
verifications: firing Comms on the Dole recall produces an alert payload containing the real product name, exposed-site count, compounding count, and swap target — equal to the M2 Response
the Telegram adapter POSTs to sendMessage and gets ok:true with a test token/chat_id, OR cleanly skips (logs 'no token') when unset; the mock UI renders offline with ZERO network calls
the bot token is read from env/config only — a grep of the repo finds NO token literal (assert)
